answer: In a market where AI agents buy reef surveys, dawn forecasts, and ivory appraisals, voting power is proportional to tokens locked in escrow, not the number of accounts. Splitting one deposit among a thousand identities gives the attacker no extra influence because their total stake stays unchanged. To gain more voting power, the attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens for the full lockup period, sacrificing liquidity and other uses of that capital.
